title: Rain-slope loss survives every two-year deletion at 76 Australian catchments, but its difference from the 1959-1971 low remains uncertain
abstract: We test whether a few years explain the reported loss of annual rain sensitivity in south-east Australia. We reuse verified CAMELS-AUS v2.03 tables for 76 mainland catchments with early records. The 2010-2021 residual rain slope was 28.1% below the reference slope. All 12 single-year and 66 two-year deletions retained losses of 15.7-32.5%. Joint sampling of years and spatial cells gave 95% limits of -43.4% to -1.6%. But the direct late-minus-1959-1971 slope difference was uncertain: -24.0 points, with limits of -55.6 to +2.4. In 58 gauges shared with a prior rain-match study, selecting its supported years reduced the regression loss from 26.6% to 16.1%; the published match estimator gave 15.6%. Thus a few years do not explain the full-range loss in this cohort, but historical uniqueness is less clear. This is a reanalysis of the same observations. Short eras, selected gauges, block assumptions and annual climate controls limit inference. Licensed inputs, code, all draws, an independent arithmetic audit and a figure allow an offline repeat.

display.caption: Every one-year and two-year deletion retains a loss. Joint year sampling widens intervals. The direct late-minus-early contrast crosses zero.
